name: VOMIT pathway
summary: Mitochondria. Valine, Odd-chain fatty acids, Methionine, Isoleucine and Threonine (VOMIT) are broken down to propionyl-CoA, which is carboxylated (biotin) and rearranged (B12) into succinyl-CoA for the TCA cycle. Propionyl-CoA carboxylase deficiency → propionic acidemia; methylmalonyl-CoA mutase or B12 deficiency → methylmalonic acidemia / raised methylmalonic acid.

valine.name: Valine
valine.notes: Branched-chain amino acid; its breakdown also needs branched-chain α-ketoacid dehydrogenase (deficient in maple syrup urine disease).

oddfa.name: Odd-chain fatty acids
oddfa.notes: β-oxidation of an odd-chain fatty acid ends with one propionyl-CoA (plus acetyl-CoAs).

methionine.name: Methionine
methionine.notes: Via SAM → homocysteine → cystathionine → α-ketobutyrate → propionyl-CoA.

isoleucine.name: Isoleucine
isoleucine.notes: Branched-chain amino acid; gives propionyl-CoA and acetyl-CoA (both glucogenic and ketogenic).

propcoa.name: Propionyl-CoA
propcoa.notes: Three-carbon acyl-CoA. Builds up in propionic acidemia.

dmmcoa.name: D-Methylmalonyl-CoA
dmmcoa.notes: The product of the carboxylase; must be converted to the L form before the mutase can use it.

lmmcoa.name: L-Methylmalonyl-CoA
lmmcoa.notes: Accumulates (and spills over as methylmalonic acid) when the mutase or B12 is lacking.

succoa.name: Succinyl-CoA
succoa.notes: Enters the TCA cycle; also used for heme synthesis (with glycine).

catab.name: Catabolism (several steps)
catab.notes: Not one enzyme: each source has its own route to propionyl-CoA. Mnemonic: VOMIT.

pcc.name: Propionyl-CoA carboxylase
pcc.notes: Biotin-dependent (like pyruvate carboxylase and acetyl-CoA carboxylase). Deficiency → propionic acidemia: poor feeding, vomiting, hypotonia, anion gap metabolic acidosis, hyperammonemia.

mcm.name: Methylmalonyl-CoA mutase
mcm.notes: Needs vitamin B12 (adenosylcobalamin). Deficiency of the enzyme or of B12 → methylmalonic acidemia; raised methylmalonic acid separates B12 deficiency from folate deficiency (both raise homocysteine).
